alignments.note: Waw rendered by the postposed *also* under rule 51; the unit is discontinuous from the waw's position under rule 25, and distance is not evidence against it.
Finite verb with its subject pronoun and auxiliary under rule 17, headed on the lexical verb under rule 24.
Object suffix realized by *them* under rule 18.
Preposition takes the written *for* under rule 11.

No conjunction morpheme stands between the two prepositional phrases, so the coordinating *and* is `added` under rule 14's closing sentences, which forbid folding such a word into the preposition standing beside it. Rule 26's `בֵּין X לְ Y` reading, which would give the *and* to the second `לְ`, was considered and set aside: that rule governs a `בֵּין` pair and a `מִן … עַד` range, and here the Hebrew merely juxtaposes a second prepositional phrase, which rule 14 names expressly.
The ASV writes nothing for this preposition's own relation, only the bare *ever* for its noun, so it is `unrepresented` under rule 40.
The indefinite article belongs to the noun that licenses it under rule 15; headed on the lexeme-bearing word.
Finite verb with subject pronoun and auxiliary under rule 17, headed on the lexical verb.
The waw's clause is recast as a relative clause with no explicit subject pronoun in it, so the waw is the morpheme licensing the relative *which* under rule 17.
Negative takes its own *not*; the ASV writes the modal and the negation as separate words, so rule 35's fused *cannot* does not arise.

Imperfect with its auxiliary and phrasal particle; *away* is a phrasal particle of the English verb under rule 44, so the head stays on *pass*. The unit is discontinuous around the negative under rule 25.

review_notes: The ASV marginal note *Or, which none shall transgress* was read and set aside; the printed text governs, by rule 38.
The only materially competing reading is the *and* of *for ever and ever*: it is marked `added` under rule 14 rather than assigned to the second `לְ` on the analogy of rule 26's `בֵּין X לְ Y`.
